name: KimaAI – AI Chatbot & Assistant for WordPress
author: nabiabdi

sections.description:
KimaAI brings modern AI features to WordPress by connecting your site to AI providers (like OpenAI) and exposing them through an easy-to-configure chatbot and a growing set of AI tools.

With KimaAI you can:

  • Build a customizable chatbot with model/provider selection, content awareness, quick actions, and an optional attention popover.
  • Add a vector database search tool and multilingual embeddings to power smarter, language-aware answers.
  • Collect chatbot feedback to understand response quality and improve your on-site experience over time.
  • Get started from Home, whose setup checklist ticks itself as you connect a provider and set up the chatbot.
  • Extend KimaAI via developer hooks/filters to register and control custom tools and tool execution.

KimaAI is built to stay flexible: it works for non-technical users who want a powerful chatbot, and it also provides hooks and internal APIs for developers who want to integrate AI deeper into their workflows.

Please make sure to carefully read the Disclaimer before using the plugin, check the KimaAI website for more information. Thank you!

Features

  • AI Chatbot: provider/model selection, content awareness, quick actions, and UI customization.
  • Home: a setup checklist, the chatbot’s status and what needs your attention.
  • Vector Search: vector DB search tool + embeddings to improve answers.
  • Multilingual-ready: multilingual embeddings and translatable dynamic settings (Polylang/WPML).
  • Feedback: collect user feedback on chatbot responses.
  • Developer hooks: register custom tools and control/observe tool calls.
  • More features coming soon!

My Vision for AI

AI is incredible, no doubt about it. It’s changing everything—from the way we work to the way we create. But for me, AI isn’t just about churning out endless content or automating everything for the sake of it. I want to see AI being used thoughtfully—as a tool that actually helps people.
I dream of an AI-driven world where creators can focus on their ideas instead of struggling with words, where language barriers don’t hold anyone back, and where tedious work is handled for us so we can spend more time on what really matters—our passions, our families, and just enjoying life.

I’ll always push for AI to be used in a way that empowers rather than overwhelms. Hope you’re with me on this! 💡💙

Disclaimer

KimaAI is a plugin that helps you to connect your websites to AI services. You need your own API keys and must follow the rules set by the AI service you choose. For OpenAI, check their Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. It is also important to check your usage on the OpenAI website for accurate information. Please do so with other services as well.

The developer of KimaAI and related parties are not responsible for any issues or losses caused by using the plugin or AI-generated content. You should talk to a legal expert and follow the laws and regulations of your country. KimaAI does only store data on your own server, and it is your responsibility to keep it safe. KimaAI’s full disclaimer is here.

External services

KimaAI connects to the services you configure. Nothing is sent until you add a service in the settings.

  • OpenAI (when you add an OpenAI environment): the visitor’s chat message, the conversation so far and the matching site content are sent to generate answers and embeddings. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • OpenRouter (when you add an OpenRouter environment): the same data, sent to the model you choose through OpenRouter. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Ollama (when you add an Ollama environment): the same data, sent to the Ollama server whose address you enter, usually your own.
  • Pinecone (premium, when you add a Pinecone embedding environment): your site content as vectors with titles, links and excerpts, and the search queries. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Qdrant (premium, when you add a Qdrant embedding environment): the same as Pinecone. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Freemius (licensing and updates): your site’s URL and plugin version for licence checks and updates, and usage data only if you opt in. Terms, Privacy Policy.

The chatbot can show a “Powered by KimaAI” link to kimaai.com in its footer. It is off unless you switch it on under Chatbot > Appearance.

Third-party resources

  • Geist Mono font by Vercel, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts/geist-mono/OFL.txt).
  • Geist font by Vercel, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts/geist/OFL.txt).
  • Vazirmatn font by Saber Rastikerdar, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/fonts/vazirmatn/OFL.txt).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/kimaai directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Open KimaAI > Home and follow the setup checklist: connect your AI provider and API key, then choose the chat model.
  4. Place the chatbot on your site and start answering visitor questions.
sections.faq:
How do I get an API key?

You can get an API key from OpenAI by creating an account on their website. Check the OpenAI website for more information.
sections.changelog:
1.6.0 – 2026-11-16

Added

  • Added (Beta): an inline chat. The new “AI chat” block, and the shortcode [kimaai_chatbot mode="inline"], place a chat inside a page’s content instead of the floating window, with its own height and greeting and a conversation of its own on each page. It works next to the floating chatbot. The block is labelled “(Beta)” in the block inserter while the feature is in beta.
  • Added Home, the new start page of KimaAI in the admin. It shows whether the chatbot is live, a setup checklist that ticks itself from your settings (connect an AI provider, choose the chat model, add your content to the knowledge base with Pro, make the chat look like your site, go live) with a link to the page of each step, what needs your attention and shortcuts. Home replaces the setup wizard: its menu entry is gone, and old links to the wizard open Home.
  • Added a search over every admin page and setting. Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux) or use the field in the top bar. Results are grouped by page, and choosing a setting opens the page and tab that hold it, scrolls to it and highlights it, opening a collapsed Advanced part when needed.
  • Added a Connections page: one page of cards for the services KimaAI connects to (AI providers, vector databases, WooCommerce and the MCP server), each with its status at a glance. Its credentials, options and connection test open in a panel, and the AI environments and vector databases are listed inside their cards.
  • Added a brand colour, four styles and a colour mode for the chatbot. You choose one brand colour and a style (Calm, Bold, Glass or Minimal), and KimaAI derives every other colour from it for light and dark mode, keeping text and controls readable to WCAG AA contrast. The colour mode is Light, Dark or Match the site, which follows the light or dark look of the page the chat sits on. A contrast report under the settings says which colours, if any, were adjusted.
  • Added new appearance settings: the launcher’s shape (circle, rounded square or with a label) and its label, a welcome heading above the greeting, the font (the site’s font by default, System or Geist), corners and density. Under Advanced, the colours of single parts (header, panel, messages, field, footer, border) can be set separately for light and dark mode (Pro), each with its contrast ratio.
  • Added a live preview beside the Appearance settings that shows the closed launcher, the welcome screen and an answer, on desktop or phone, and in light or dark mode.
  • Added an AI notice to the chatbot (“You’re chatting with an AI assistant.”), so visitors know they are talking to an AI, as the EU AI Act (Article 50) asks. It is on by default, on existing sites too, shows before consent and in the attention popover as well, and its text and switch are in the Appearance settings.
  • Added masking of payment card numbers and IBANs. They are replaced in visitors’ messages and in tool results before anything reaches the AI provider, and they are not stored. It is on by default under Privacy and security. An optional setting also hides email addresses and phone numbers from the AI provider, while the chat history and handoffs keep them. The MCP server’s redaction masks card numbers and IBANs too.
  • Added code blocks with a language label and their own copy button to chatbot answers. A long line scrolls sideways, the block can be reached by keyboard, and “Copied” is announced to screen readers.

Changed

  • Redesigned the KimaAI admin as one app with a sidebar that can be collapsed: Home; Chatbot (Appearance, Behaviour, Quick actions, Conversations); Knowledge (Sources and sync, Content templates, Pinned answers, Glossary, Quality); Feedback Analytics; Connections; and Settings (Privacy and security, Usage and cost, Function tools, MCP server, Logs, Data and export, About). WordPress notices are shown inside the app, and old links to settings pages and to the feedback analytics keep working.
  • Settings pages are now cards of setting rows, with rarely used settings in a collapsed Advanced part. Each page has its own Save and Reset in its header and a floating save bar once a long page has scrolled, and leaving a page with unsaved changes asks first. The entries of a list, such as quick actions, glossary terms or AI environments, open in a side panel or a dialog and save only that list.
  • The admin now uses the Geist font (Geist Mono for code and version numbers), Yekan for Persian and Vazirmatn for Arabic, all shipped with the plugin. Its dark mode uses KimaAI’s brand palette, the light and dark switch sits in the top bar, and WordPress notices in the app follow the mode.
  • Pro features now carry one “Pro” badge on menus, pages, sections and fields instead of “PRO feature.” in their text, and a Pro page on a free install shows one short upgrade panel with the badge and the upgrade button.
  • Redesigned the chat widget: a launcher with the KimaAI mark or your own icon that stays as a close button while the chat is open, the attention popover as one card, a window that rises from the launcher and fills the screen on phones, a header with a menu (new conversation, larger window), a welcome screen, a thinking line while it answers, Stop while an answer streams, errors as a card with Try again, reasons and a comment for “Not helpful”, the consent request as a card above the field, the end-of-chat rating as a sheet inside the window instead of a dialog over it, dividers between days, tables, and a message field that grows with the text. Product cards are now the chatbot’s own cards in a scrolling row and keep WooCommerce’s Add to cart, Select options or View.
  • Existing sites keep their look. On update, each site’s appearance carries over to the Bold style with its own colours, the corner shapes and depth of its previous style, its chat icon, avatar and texts. Where an old colour pair failed the contrast rules, such as white text on a light brand colour, the text colour is adjusted. Choosing a style on the Appearance page ends the old shapes. The previous settings are kept, so a downgrade to 1.5.x still shows the old look.
  • New sites start with the Calm style in light mode, KimaAI’s brand colour, the KimaAI mark on the launcher and a spark beside answers, and with new default texts: “AI assistant” under the chatbot’s name, the heading “Hi, how can I help?” and a shorter greeting. The previous chat icons are under “More icons”. Existing sites keep their stored texts and icon and get no heading.
  • The chatbot now renders in an isolated part of the page (a shadow root), so a theme’s or another plugin’s CSS can no longer change how it looks, and its message field no longer shows in a monospace font. It uses the site’s font by default. Forms from Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms and WooCommerce product HTML shown in the chat keep the site’s styles and scripts.
  • The launcher’s distance from the edges of the screen is now free; it was Pro. The colours of single parts of the chat are a Pro setting now: colours an existing free site set keep showing until they are changed.
  • The “Powered by KimaAI” link in the chatbot is now opt-in, off by default and marked nofollow, as WordPress.org’s guidelines ask. Because a stored “on” could not be told apart from the old default, the update turns it off on every site; switch it on again under Appearance if you want to show it.
  • Content awareness is now on by default for new installs; existing installs keep their setting. It reads the page the visitor is on only on single posts and pages, so on search results and archives it no longer takes one of the listed posts for that page. The section the visitor is reading now comes first in {post_content} and is available on its own as the new {post_section} placeholder.
  • Links to your own site in chatbot answers now open in the same tab; links to other sites still open in a new tab.
  • API keys and other secrets are no longer sent to the browser. A saved key shows as “Saved” with Replace and Remove, a duplicated AI environment or vector database starts without its key, and a connection test uses the saved key only with the provider and address it was saved with.
  • Posts that are not public are no longer added to the knowledge base: drafts, private and password-protected posts, and posts restricted by MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro or LearnDash. After the update, a background job adds to each existing vector who may see its post, without re-embedding, and removes the vectors of posts that may no longer be indexed. Until it has finished, each search result is still checked before use.
  • PDFs larger than 20 MB are now skipped during a sync, with the reason in the log, instead of being read whole into memory.
  • WordPress 6.6 is now the minimum version: the plugin’s scripts need the React JSX runtime that WordPress ships since 6.6, so 1.5.13 already failed to load them on WordPress 6.0 to 6.5. KimaAI is tested up to WordPress 7.1.
  • Requests to AI providers now go through the WordPress HTTP API, like other plugins’ requests. Streamed answers still use cURL, because the HTTP API cannot pass on a response while it arrives.
  • On sites with WPML or Polylang, the visitor-facing texts of list entries are now translated per entry: the label and message of each quick action, the approved wording of each glossary term and the answer of each pinned answer. Glossary notes and the questions and phrasings of pinned answers are no longer translated, because visitors’ questions are matched against them in one language.

Improved

  • Conversations is now an inbox: a searchable list grouped by day with the first question, the page, the number of questions and the ratings of each conversation, beside the open transcript. An answer’s details (sources, model and token usage, tool calls, and the raw request and response) open in a side panel.
  • Sources and sync now says in one verdict whether the knowledge base works (healthy, needs attention or not working) and why. Health lists one row per check with what it found, the fix and a button to where it is made, and keeps the raw figures behind Details. It now counts failed items apart from content changed since its sync.
  • The Logs page is now a log viewer: entries newest first with their level and time, filters by level, a search, and details with the source, file and line and any JSON body pretty-printed. The log files are listed beside it with their day and size.
  • The Feedback Analytics page now shows answer ratings and conversation ratings in one list with filters and a search, beside the figures, the ratings per day and the satisfaction scores. A rating opens with its conversation in a side panel, and the list exports what its filters select as CSV.
  • On sites with WPML or Polylang, the top bar shows the language you are editing and the default language, and every translatable text has a line that links to its translation in WPML or Polylang. Outside the default language these texts are read-only.
  • Deleting a vector collection and revoking an MCP access token now ask for confirmation first, and show a failure in the dialog.
  • Improved the chatbot’s accessibility, checked against WCAG 2.2 AA: links in answers meet AA contrast and are underlined, keyboard focus stays inside the chat’s dialogs, Escape closes an open rating sheet before the window, the keyboard hint of the message field is read by screen readers, and the waiting button’s accessible name includes the time it shows.
  • On right-to-left sites, the messages, the message field, the header and the attention popover now mirror; the launcher and the window stay on the side set in the settings.

Fixed

  • Fixed streamed answers ending empty when the model still asked for tools after the last allowed round of tool calls. A streamed answer now gets a final answer in that case, as one that does not stream already did: the pending tool calls are not run, and the model answers with what it has.
  • Fixed knowledge base searches on Qdrant returning nothing. Results were read in Pinecone’s format only, so a site on Qdrant got no knowledge in the chatbot’s answers, no vector results in the hybrid search and no rows from wp kimaai vectors query. Qdrant results now reach all of them.
  • Fixed Qdrant errors losing their reason: a wrong vector size, for example, now says which dimensions were expected and which were sent instead of only “HTTP 400 error”.
  • Fixed deleting the embeddings of a long post leaving vectors behind. Only its first 200 chunks were read, so the rest stayed in the vector database. All of them are deleted now, and a failed request stops the delete and shows the error instead of reading as the end of the list.
  • Fixed tool calls on Ollama repeating until the round limit ran out. Ollama ignores the reference to the previous response, so after a tool call the model saw only the tool’s result, without the question. The conversation is now sent again with each continuation.
  • Fixed WooCommerce product cards missing from answers given on Ollama.
  • Fixed the WooCommerce tools failing when their instructions setting had never been saved.
  • Fixed database schema changes never reaching existing tables. The table definitions were written in a form WordPress’s table updater could not read, so columns added by an update were not added to tables that already existed.
  • Fixed network-activated installs on multisite: a new site of the network gets its tables at once instead of when its admin is first opened, and uninstalling removes each site’s data when that site’s setting asks for it.
  • Fixed content awareness failing on hosts without PHP’s intl extension.
  • Fixed the satisfaction survey coming back every time the chat was closed after the visitor chose “Not now”. It now stays away for that conversation and asks again in a new one.
  • Fixed list items written with a plus sign (“+ item”) keeping the “+” in their text.
  • Fixed the [kimaai_chatbot] shortcode printing a second chatbot when the chatbot is already shown on every page. Without a mode it now prints the floating chat once, or nothing when it is on for the whole site, and it loads the chatbot’s scripts wherever it is placed.
  • Fixed the settings screen hanging on “Saving…” or on loading after a failed request. The error now shows as a notice that can be dismissed.
  • Fixed settings added by a plugin update staying empty in the admin until the page was reloaded.
  • Fixed the knowledge base query highlighting nothing in its results when a query of several words had no exact match. The single words are highlighted now.
  • Fixed a failed sync row showing the error of an earlier status request instead of its own sync error.
  • Fixed importing a settings export emptying every AI and vector database key. The export leaves keys blank, and the import wrote the blanks over the stored keys; a blank or missing key now keeps the stored one, and a key in the file still replaces it.
  • Fixed the WPML configuration file (wpml-config.xml) missing from the plugin’s zip files, so WPML did not offer KimaAI’s texts for translation.
  • Fixed MCP audit log entries and groundedness log answers being lost when a long text was cut in the middle of a multibyte character. They are now cut by characters, not bytes.
  • Fixed PHP warnings on every request of the feedback overview without a rating filter, and for an unknown integration key.

Removed

  • Removed the Replicate provider, its models and settings. On update, Replicate AI environments are removed. A chatbot that ran on Replicate is switched off on every page and stays set to the removed environment, shown as “no longer available”, so visitors’ messages never go to a provider you did not choose; select another AI environment to switch it on again.
  • Removed the “Include sensitive data” option of the settings export: an export never contains API keys. An import on the same site keeps the stored keys; on another site, enter them again.
  • Removed the kimaai_chatbot_allowed filter, deprecated since 1.3.5. Use kimaai_chatbot_gate.
  • Removed the kimaai_is_premium and kimaai_can_use_premium_code filters, which only worked on KimaAI’s own test setups. No filter can turn on premium code any more.

Security

  • Fixed the chatbot running a tool that had not been offered to the AI model for that request. A crafted message could make the model name another tool. The chatbot now refuses every tool call outside the tools it offered, and reports the refusal to the model as an error.
  • Password-protected posts are kept out of the knowledge base. They were embedded and could be quoted in answers. Syncs skip them, a post that gets a password loses its vectors (so do its attachments), existing vectors are removed by the index maintenance, and a post is embedded again once its password is removed. The chatbot’s post tools refuse them too.
  • Content awareness now leaves out password-protected posts for every visitor, so the text of such a page no longer reaches the AI provider or the stored conversation once a visitor has entered its password.
  • The chatbot’s post tools, its keyword search and content awareness now use a post only for a visitor who may see it on the site: never drafts, private or password-protected posts, and content restricted by MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro or LearnDash only for those who have access. Each knowledge base result is checked the same way before it is used.
  • A conversation held by a logged-in user can no longer be read, continued or rated by another user or a visitor. Logging out clears the chatbot’s session cookie, and logging in starts a new session.
  • Custom PHP tools now need permission to edit code. Only users with the edit_plugins capability can save a tool’s code, the saved code is signed, and tools run only with a valid signature and while DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT is off. Existing custom PHP tools stay off until an administrator who may edit plugins saves the function tools settings again.
  • The visitor’s IP address is now read from the connection itself, not from headers a visitor can send, which could be used to get round an IP ban or the daily message limit. Sites behind a load balancer, reverse proxy or CDN list its addresses with the new kimaai_trusted_proxies filter; until then, all visitors share the proxy’s address for these limits.
  • Fixed banned IP ranges matching only their first address, an IP check turning a banned-word block back into “allowed”, and a trailing comma in the banned words list blocking every message.
  • The public feedback routes now take one rating per answer and a satisfaction rating only for a conversation that exists, so scripts can no longer flood the feedback analytics or the human handoff.
  • wp kimaai vectors config get now masks the vector database’s API key instead of printing it in plain text.
  • Hardened the plugin’s output: the chatbot’s root element, streamed event names and error messages are escaped, and the remaining PHP files exit when loaded outside WordPress.

Developer

  • Every public hook now has a page on kimaai.com/docs/hooks/ with its parameters, when it fires and a tested example. Public hooks are kept stable; a hook marked @internal in the code may change without notice.
  • kimaai_chatbot_error and kimaai_chatbot_after_response now fire for streamed answers too, with the same arguments as for answers that do not stream. An error the provider reports in the stream has the new code ai_stream_error.
  • kimaai_chatbot_handoff passes a fourth argument, $ticket, with the channel, reference and url of the handoff. Callbacks written for three arguments keep working.
  • Added the kimaai:chatbot browser event for analytics and Google Tag Manager. It is sent on the chat’s root element, bubbles and crosses the widget’s shadow root, so listeners on document and window get it, for open, close, message, answer and feedback, with the session ID and, for feedback, the rating. It never carries what the visitor typed.
  • Added the kimaai_chatbot_csat_saved action, which fires when a visitor’s rating of a whole conversation was saved, and kimaai_embedding_index_changed, which fires when chunks are stored in or removed from the knowledge base, so caches built on it can be cleared.
  • Added the kimaai_embedding_pdf_max_bytes filter for the largest PDF read for the knowledge base, 20 MB by default.
  • kimaai_trigger_button_click now passes the key of the button’s field in its second argument, so an add-on with several buttons knows which one was clicked.
  • kimaai_tool_call_allowed is now asked once for every tool call the chatbot makes, not only for Pro’s function tools, and a blocked call runs nothing. kimaai_chatbot_max_tool_rounds now applies to streamed answers too and counts the rounds after the first reply on both paths; 0 runs no tool.
  • kimaai_chatbot_theme_vars now receives the variables of the new theme engine for each colour mode, with the look and the mode as new arguments; names it sets from before 1.6.0 still take effect. kimaai_chatbot_theme_styles and kimaai_chatbot_color_presets are now internal and only affect how an existing site’s look carries over.
  • Deprecated kimaai_chatbot_theme (use kimaai_chatbot_theme_vars) and kimaai_stream_tool_call (use kimaai_chatbot_tool_call). Both keep working with WordPress’s deprecation notice until their removal in 1.8.0. The internal filters kimaai_assistant_history_model, kimaai_assistant_history_context, kimaai_assistant_persisted_renderables and kimaai_assistant_hydrated_renderables are now kimaai_chat_*; the old names still run, with a notice.
  • kimaai_settings_schema_files can add settings files but no longer remove KimaAI’s own, and a setting stays secret when any file marks it. kimaai_chatbot_daily_message_limit is now always a whole number of 0 or more.
  • wp kimaai db scenario and wp kimaai db run are now available only on KimaAI’s own test sites; they were meant for testing migrations.
  • Added wp kimaai vectors backfill-access, which adds to existing vectors who may see their post without re-embedding, and wp kimaai vectors freshness counts the vectors still without it.
  • Fixed wp kimaai vectors delete: --filter deleted nothing on Qdrant, a delete without --ids, --filter or --all reached the vector database, --all failed on Qdrant, and a delete left the local index rows behind, so a later sync never uploaded those chunks again.
  • Fixed wp kimaai vectors sync --post_type=post,page syncing nothing; a comma-separated list of post types now works.
  • Fixed wp kimaai vectors fetch showing no payload on Qdrant, wp kimaai vectors items get printing PHP’s export format instead of JSON, wp kimaai vectors items list --format=json and --format=csv adding a total line that broke the output, and an unknown --env in wp kimaai vectors config and collections ending in a PHP fatal error instead of a WP-CLI error.
  • Fixed wp kimaai chat stopping after 15 messages a day: all chats from WP-CLI shared one visitor counter. It is now exempt from the visitor limit, as wp kimaai eval is.
  • Fixed wp kimaai run printing 22 synopsis warnings on every run and wp kimaai chat printing two warnings when started without --session-id.
  • Fixed the help texts of the wp kimaai vectors commands: the examples named wp vectors, items list documented the wrong page size and the collections examples used the wrong option.

For the full changelog, visit:
https://kimaai.com/changelog/

screenshots.caption: The chatbot in light and dark mode, side by side.
The chatbot answering visitors on your site, from your own content.
The chat block: a chat right inside a page (Beta).
Home with the setup checklist: provider, chat model, content, look and going live.
Appearance: brand colour, style and colour mode, with a live preview of the chatbot.
Connections: AI providers, vector databases and plugins in one place.
Content awareness: the chatbot answers from the page the visitor is reading.
Quick actions: one-click buttons for common questions (Pro).
Knowledge, Sources and sync: which content is in the vector database (Pro).
Conversations: every chat with its transcript, model, tokens and ratings.
Feedback Analytics: helpful answers, CSAT scores and visitor comments (Pro).
Function tools: your own PHP functions the chatbot may call (Pro).
MCP server: connect an AI agent with scoped access tokens (Pro).
Search every setting and page with Ctrl K or Cmd K.
The admin in dark mode: quick actions next to the live preview (Pro).
